High level asks from our side: 1) can you invoice as a single annual invoice or do you prefer staged invoices? 2) what supporting docs do you provide for the EU VAT reverse-charge / reclaim? 3) how do we trigger drawdowns against the committed balance (monthly windows, thresholds, PO required)?

We have an internal procurement cutoff on the 20th of the month, so if there's a typical lead time for PO + wire, please make that explicit.

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Annual committed spend — invoicing & drawdown approach

Hi Clara — thanks for the clear list. Below is a proposed approach that aligns with how other EU customers operate and keeps your procurement window in mind. TL;DR: we can issue either a single annual invoice (preferred for accounting simplicity) or 4 quarterly invoices; drawdowns are initiated by a simple monthly withdrawal request tied to PO/GL reference.

Proposal (preferred):
- Invoice: single annual invoice for the committed amount (one line item: Redwood Inference Annual Committed Capacity). Payment term: Net 30.
- Drawdown cadence: Clearsky submits a monthly "withdrawal request" email by the 3rd of each month with PO or internal reference; Redwood executes token / capacity allocation within 5 business days and sends a drawdown confirmation email with a running ledger balance.
- Threshold gating: For security & finance control we recommend a rolling minimum balance of 15% of committed value to remain on account. If balance falls below this, automated notification + 7 business day window to top up; failure to top up triggers temporary capacity hold (grace period).
- VAT evidence: we will provide an invoice in your requested format, plus: (1) our company VAT registration (Redwood B.V. EU VAT ID), (2) statement of services rendered linked to invoice line items, and (3) if reverse-charge applies, we include the standard reverse-charge notice on the invoice. For reclaim you will have the invoice + our VAT id — you indicated you expect to reverse-charge on your filings.
- Attachments: sample invoice template attached (PDF).

Operational next steps (if you approve):
1) Clearsky returns signed PO (we can accept scanned PDF) and bank remit details.
2) We issue the annual invoice and send DocuSign link for the Master Purchase Schedule (DocuSign for signatures optional).
3) First drawdown request processed after payment reaches our account (or we can accept pre-payment confirmation for allocation).

I've looped in Kimberly (tax & billing ops) and Marissa (account lead) — Kimberly, can you confirm the exact VAT phrasing we put on the invoice for Clearsky EU reverse-charge?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_Invoice_Sample_AnnualPrepay_v2.pdf (pdf)]

Hi Clara — quick note on VAT phrasing (confirming what Jonas suggested):

1) Invoice will include: our EU VAT ID (NL/BE/IE depending on entity used), line item descriptions, and the phrase: "VAT reverse charge applies per Article 194 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC" (or local language if preferred).
2) For your reclaim: you will receive the signed invoice, bank remittance confirmation (once payment clears), and a short statement of services (1 page) that ties the invoice to usage.
3) If your AP team requires additional detail (e.g., GL codes, cost centers), include a short CSV template and we can populate per invoice.

About drawdown gating: we can automate the rolling min-balance monitoring and produce a monthly ledger CSV with token-level consumption and remaining committed credit. That feed will be pushed to a secure S3 bucket link you control (we can also deliver via emailed CSV if preferred).

Let us know whether you want a single-file invoice or quarterly billing. If single invoice, we will mark the invoice note: "Prepaid capacity — non-refundable except as specified in contract" and include the drawdown trigger instructions.

Kimberly Park
Billing & Tax Manager
Redwood Inference
